reasoning: Recent polling in Florida over the last 45 days contains at least one clear, in-state general-election Senate poll and no fresh general-election presidential polling. The University of North Florida/Public Opinion Research Lab survey from July 8–17, 2026 shows Republican Sen. Ashley Moody leading both Democratic challengers by mid–single to low–double digits, indicating a current Republican advantage of roughly R+8 to R+10 in the Senate race. Structurally, Florida’s Cook PVI of about R+5 reinforces that the state leans Republican, so in the absence of contrary presidential head-to-head polling in this window, the best-supported quantitative signal is that the Senate race currently favors Republicans by mid–single digits, while the presidential landscape is at least modestly R-leaning but not directly polled in this period.

sources.name: WUWF / University of North Florida PORL
sources.details: University of North Florida’s Public Opinion Research Lab poll of 848 likely Florida midterm voters found Republican Sen. Ashley Moody leading Democrat Angie Nixon 50%-42% (Moody +8) and leading Democrat Alexander Vindman 50%-40% (Moody +10) in general-election Senate matchups.

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.details: Coverage of the Democratic Senate primary notes Angie Nixon’s 56.1%-43.9% win over Alexander Vindman but does not provide any general-election polling against Republican Sen. Ashley Moody.
sources.date_range: August 18, 2026 (reported; primary results, not a general-election poll window)

sources.name: Eciks summary of James Madison Institute poll
sources.details: A James Madison Institute/Targoz Market Research poll (reported in secondary coverage) primarily measured the 2026 Florida GOP governor primary and included general-election governor matchups showing Republican Byron Donalds leading Democrat David Jolly by 7 points (45%-38%), suggesting a broader Republican advantage in statewide races but not directly measuring the Senate or presidential race.

sources.name: The New York Times
sources.details: An article on Florida’s polling landscape compiles several July 2026 surveys, but these focus on the gubernatorial GOP primary and do not provide general-election Senate or presidential head-to-heads; they nonetheless underscore strong Republican positioning in statewide contests.
sources.date_range: Late July 2026 (article summarizing multiple July polls)

sources.name: Cook Partisan Voting Index (via summary table)
sources.details: Cook Partisan Voting Index lists Florida as R+5 at the statewide level, reflecting that in the last two presidential elections the state voted about 5 points more Republican than the national average; this is a structural baseline, not a 2026 race poll.
